\section[\texorpdfstring{\te{మొండి} (moṇḍi)}{మొండి (moṇḍi)}]{\te{మొండి} (moṇḍi) — stubborn}

\label{lesson:TE-C297-mondi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for useful, then the Telugu for local.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{మొండి}}
\textbf{\te{మొండి}} — \emph{moṇḍi} — \textquotedblleft{}stubborn\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\te{మొండి}} (\emph{moṇḍi}) is native Dravidian. DEDR 5114 lists \emph{moṇḍi}, \textquotedblleft{}maimed, blunt, stubborn\textquotedblright{}, with Kannada \emph{moṇḍa}, \textquotedblleft{}blunt, maimed\textquotedblright{}. DEDR compares Sanskrit \emph{muṇḍa}, \textquotedblleft{}hornless, blunt\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}
